_note: Hand-annotated expectations for offline evaluation. Ground truth is what a competent adjuster would conclude from the photo, not what any model said. Keep assertions to things the image clearly supports.

cases.notes: Renault Megane Mk1 hit a tree head-on. Bumper detached, hood folded, windshield shattered, door aperture sprung -- structural.

Side impact: front door skin and fender creased, window taped over. Panel damage only, no structural deformation. A competent adjuster writes this off on economics rather than severity: door plus fender work on a 1999 Escort exceeds what the car is worth. Previously left unasserted, which meant the headline verdict on this case was never graded.
Severe frontal collision, front clip destroyed, wheel displaced, glass shattered. Clear total loss on an old vehicle.

Late-model silver sedan, front-quarter impact. Front fender creased and the bumper corner scuffed and dented; headlight and glass intact, wheel and suspension undisturbed. Unambiguously a repair on a car of this value. The set had no confirmed not-a-total-loss case, so nothing was testing whether the cost-vs-value rule over-writes-off healthy vehicles.

Manufacturer press photo of an intact car in motion. No damage of any kind. A negative control: the set had none, so nothing tested whether the detector invents damage regions and a repair cost on a clean vehicle. Motion blur and dappled forest light are exactly the conditions that produce false positives.
